text:
Kevin Fiala played his first NHL game in nine months on Thursday, and the Kings still lost. Fiala broke his left leg in several places playing for Switzerland at the Olympics in February, needed a second surgery in September, and came back with a power-play assist in 16:37 against the Islanders, per ESPN. It was also Darcy Kuemper's 500th NHL game, and a Yahoo Sports headline summed up the night: a huge milestone for Kuemper, a brutal result for the Kings. Los Angeles lost 5-2 and has 12 points in 17 games.

Here's the thing Peter Laviolette's team can hold onto: the Kings have been better than their record by a distance. They're minus-13 in goal difference on chances worth plus-3.1, with 51% of the expected goals, our measure of chance quality. Finishing has cost them 6.6 goals and goaltending 9.4. Over a three-game winless run they had 57% of the expected goals and were outscored 13-4. Kuemper, projected to start again, has stopped .847 over his last five starts, 6.4 goals worse than expected. With Fiala and Artemi Panarin finally in the same lineup (Panarin arrived from the Rangers in February), the scoring finally has more help. Fiala is one assist from 300, Quinton Byfield two points from 200, and 41-year-old Corey Perry is one of our Sleepers on the strength of his shot quality.

Calgary opens a three-game road trip without Kevin Bahl, who is out for the season after surgery for a ruptured Achilles, per the Flames. He led the team in ice time. Zayne Parekh has been the good news, a defenseman Daily Faceoff says is blossoming into a star, and Matt Coronato is one goal from 50 for his career. Dustin Wolf, though, is 6.6 goals worse than expected this season, so both starters tonight have been well below average.

Our numbers have the Kings at 3.25 expected goals to Calgary's 2.68. Los Angeles still has a 28% playoff chance by our count; Calgary is at 10%.
headline: Kings get Fiala back, still waiting for saves
